I've completed testing as persona **anna** (retired teacher, 68, font scale 1.3×, small Android 11 phone, en-GB). The result is a complete blocker — here's my full report.

## What happened

The app (`si.flisk.chat`) is a Capacitor WebView shell that loads `https://chat.flisk.si` as a remote URL (see `testers/chat-wrapper/capacitor.config.json`). When I opened it on the Android emulator, the screen stayed **completely blank** for the entire test — no welcome heading, no message input, no example chips, no sign-in button. Nothing tappable ever appeared.

I tried:
- Waiting 30+ seconds across multiple screenshots
- Force-stopping and restarting the app
- Swiping up/down and tapping various screen areas
- Checking ADB logs and window state

## Root cause

The emulator has **no network connectivity at all**. Every destination is unreachable — `chat.flisk.si`, `google.com`, and even `1.1.1.1` all return "Destination Host Unreachable" via gateway `10.0.2.2`. Since the WebView can't fetch the remote page, nothing renders. There's also no offline fallback or "no internet" error banner shown to the user.

## Files written (per AGENT_BRIEF.md)

- `results/anna/report.md` — full QA report with severity ratings
- `results/anna/findings.json` — machine-readable findings

## Findings

| # | Title | Severity | Screens |
|---|-------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Blank screen — app never loads (no network) | blocker | 01–14 |
| 2 | Cannot ask Flisk Chat anything — no input renders | blocker | 01–14 |

## Anna's verdict

**Score: 0/10** — would not keep the app. The screen is blank with no explanation, no retry button, and no way to type anything. A retired teacher with low patience for jargon would have no idea what's wrong and would delete it immediately.

## Important caveat

This blocker is the **test environment's network**, not necessarily a defect in the app itself. On a device with working network, the WebView should load `chat.flisk.si` normally and anna's mission (ask a real question, follow up once, judge usefulness) should be completable. The app needs re-testing once the emulator can reach the network.

I did not sign in with GitHub, type any real email, or enter credentials — as required for signed-out testing.
